Security Companies: Private protection or a Trojan Horse?

By: Johann Botha | Production

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
Every month you pay a security company to guard you and your belongings. But can you trust them implicitly? Carte Blanche investigates three unrelated Johannesburg robberies that seem to have a lot more in common than meets the eye.

Summary:
The private security industry in South Africa ranks among the largest in the world, with over 9,000 registered companies to choose from, 450,000 registered active private security guards and a further 1.5 million qualified (but inactive) guards. Far outnumbering the available personnel than the combined South African police and army. Studies have shown that South Africa had 2.57 private security personnel for every police employee.

In South Africa, the high levels of crime and inability of the police to curb its upward trend, has lead many South African households to fork out thousands of rands every year to keep their assets safe. But are they?

There is no doubt its a lucrative industry to be in. In fact, in SA it is in excess of R30 billion annually (as per surveys done in 2012). But are these private security companies contributing to combatting the insecurities it aims to address or are they exacerbating the problem and perpetuating the fear?

We take a look at one such private security firm who is accused of facilitating break-ins, blocking paying clients' phones (preventing alarm signals to go through) and "scouting" potential targets before they get hit. All our case studies recounts the exact same modus operandi, indicates the same individual involved in the robberies and all of them lost a significant amount of stock and personal belongings.

Case Study:
Jacqui Faucitt CEO Regima South Africa
Mike Ryan Owner of Ryan's Nursery
Kerry Albertyn Owner Supa Quick

Expert:
Ms. Brigadier Mathapelo Peters Brigadier Peters SAPS
Mr. Emmet O'Rafferty Owner Top Security

Locations:
Bedfordview

Other Footage Sources:
Security Camera footage provided by some of the victims

Legal: Yes
Reason for legal: To advise on allegations levelled against security company as well as certain individuals working for the security firm.
The owner of the implicated security firm did not sign the release form, instead he provided a letter to cover the details specified in the release form. Legal has to advise how to react to this letter and how this letter has bearing on broadcasting the on-camera interview done with the owner

Press Release:


Security Breaches
Every month you pay a security company to guard you and your belongings. But can you trust them implicitly? Carte Blanche investigates three unrelated Johannesburg robberies that seem to have a lot more in common than meets the eye.


Script:


Kerry Late Saturday night, I must have had 50 plus missed calls, from an unknown number. One after the other, just random – call after call after call after call.
Mike There were approximately a 125 calls made to my phone.
Jackie From 9 0 clock myself and my husband our phones, our cell phones started to go. Until after two in the morning. So, more than 5 hours.
"All three of these business owners from Bedfordview in Johannesburg, were robbed last year. In all three cases the owners’ phones were mysteriously flooded, with hundreds of calls from unknown numbers, for hours during the course of the robberies.
It is standard procedure to supply your chosen security company with one or more numbers which they then phone when your alarm goes off. If they don't get hold of you, they send their armed response officers to go and investigate. Or so the theory goes…in these 3 cases the security company could not get through to alert them of the alarm activations. "

And when their teams went out to the premises they did not see anything suspicious
Kerry They are supposed to get to the gate, contact security, security allows them access to my premises. They then inspect the building that I pay them for. I don't pay them to get to the gate and then leave, I pay them to come and inspect the premises. If there's a problem at the premises, they then contact us. They got to the gate, turned around and went away.

All three businesses used Top Security. The CEO of Top Security denies any involvement by his company and employees in these three incidents.
O Rafferty It is typical for people to blame the security man, automatically – evidence or no evidence.
"But in this case, their suspicions might be more than a knee-jerk reaction, because they share some interesting similarities.
In all three cases the robbers knew exactly how to get in, where the alarm system was located and they were in no hurry to get out, even after the alarms were triggered.
Kerry owns Supa Quick. Here they entered through the only window not covered by a beam, and as if they knew there was a beam just outside an interleading door, they went straight into the ceiling and crawled two rooms across before coming down exactly where the alarm box was."
kerry So, how convenient that they knew exactly where to climb in, exactly where to climb out, to destroy this? Do me a favour...
At Mike Ryan's nursery they cleared the hardware store, mostly of equipment robbers would use.
Mike Two key cutting machines were standing here. One was here, and one was over here.
"They also took angle grinders, chain saws and generators, spending about 4 hours in his nursery, despite the alarm going off twice.
"
Mike They were completely relaxed while they were shopping
The robbers were so relaxed, they even spent time in the restaurant area and drank the expensive whisky Mike kept in his office. At Supa Quick they did the same.
Kerry They spent 4 hours here. They sat at this desk, the robbers, they drank our whisky, with milk.
"Both Mike and Kerry had their own on-site guards, who were meant to open for the response officers. But because they were being held at gunpoint by the robbers, they couldn’t. Mike feels that their absence should have been seen as suspicious. But in both cases the officer simply claimed that he couldn't get access or see anything unusual.
"
O Rafferty We did an investigation, and we didn't see anything untoward in what he did in his routing that night
' – and yet the locked gate where the officer would have stopped, was cut open by the robbers and their 5 ton truck, was parked in clear view of the gate.
Mike The security company claims that they never saw the truck, but the truck is parked where that Nissan is parked, and as you can see it's quite visible from this area.
Phone flooding is a new technique used by criminals, but it also points a finger at the security company. Only the owners and the security company know which numbers are to be phoned when the alarm is triggered. In Mike's case, Top Security had four contact numbers. But only 2 of them were flooded, and as it happened, Top Security also only tried to phone these same 2 numbers when the alarm went off.
Mike Only two of the numbers were blocked, the other numbers were still open, but were not called by Top Security.
In the third case, involving Jackie Fawcet's wellness centre, Top security had three numbers, one of which was originally written down incorrectly on the contract, and this unrelated number was also flooded on the night of the robbery.
Jackie So that was a total stranger. We don't know that person, we don't know where they are in SA. That cannot be, those three numbers, given by anybody else, in the world.
But Mr o Rafferty says she also had a copy of the contract.
O Rafferty So anybody who accessed their records, would have also had the same numbers.
Jackie We have a safe where we keep all documentation, so it's impossible.
We tracked down a cyber criminal who explained how flooding works.
Hacker You need to obtain the phone numbers of the person being flooded from someone inside the security company. From there you go to the dark web where you can hire a company who then flood that cell phone number for the next hour, two hours, by paying them an hourly rate per number.
One particular employee, called Lucky, stands out in two of these cases. He was the response officer who did not see the truck, or the open gate at Mike's nursery. And a week before the robbery at the wellness centre, he enquired at the sports shop in the same building about the cost of a kitting out an entire soccer team from head to toe – an unusual request from any customer. He also had a look at the stock room to see if they had the right kit. On the night of the break in, the robbers smashed their way through the top floor balcony door, ignored all the expensive computers and other equipment and stole only the soccer gear. Lucky was not on duty that and the officers who responded walked around the building, and said the saw nothing out of the ordinary.
Jackie
O Rafferty We gave him a polygraph, which he passed
Jackie says, shortly after she accused him, he tried to intimidate her
Jackie Two weeks after the robbery, 3 o clock in the morning, the intercom goes. So I answer it, and this man says, it's Lucky from Top Security. I put the intercom down and I phoned the call centre of the security company immediately and I said, have you had any alarm calls from my home adress? Nothing!
Jackie suggests that perhaps mr O Rafferty simply does not know about the involvement of some of his staff members in these robberies, but he disagrees.
O Rafferty Yes there was a robbery, and these people incurred a loss, but it wasn't us.
Jackie Really, I think he's delusional when he thinks that there is not a conspiracy going on within his company.
On the night of Kerry's robbery at Supa-Quick, according to the tied up guard's affidavit, one of the robbers phoned someone when Top Security arrived at the gate and complained that they sent out the wrong person...
O'Rafferty Why, why, why is the security guard suddenly the bastion of truthfulness, and we're not?
Lucky has since left Top Security
O rafferty He didn't leave us under a cloud, if that's your question. I can't give you the exact details, but he didn't leave under a cloud.
We tried to convince Lucky to speak to us, but, in spite of all our messages and phone calls, he would not grant us an interview, claiming he is innocent, saying he’s already given his affidavits to the police.
Lucky And I’ve even told Top Security they mustn't phone me anymore. I don't have to deal with them. Thank you, bye bye.
Somehow, the investigations into all three of these cases were closed by Bedfordview police for lack of evidence, even though they lost the security camera footage Mike supplied – more than once...
Mike We phoned and asked what was happening with the case, and they said that they'd lost the disk, could we please give them another one. So I said yes, I had another disk which I gave to them, and they seemingly have lost that one as well.
The two eyewitness reports also disappeared from the dossier. When Bedfordview police refused to speak to us, we went to the provincial head office.
Brigadier When Carte blanche contacted me, obviously then I checked with the provincial head of detectives what is the status of these cases. We sat together, we investigated and explored, and we realised that perhaps not enough was done, so we immediately gave an instruction that the cases should be re-opened for further investigation.
Claire Some complainants say that they suspect the police to be involved?
Brigadier They will be investigated disciplinary, ag internally, and disciplinary steps will be taken against any members, should they be found guilty of any misconduct.
Kerry I've been involved in a shooting incident twice in my life, where i've been shot in robberies. Ive been shot through both my legs, i've been shot through my fingers, in my forehead and in my chest. If the guardians of our community are the robbers, it's never going to stop. And we've got a responsibility to stop the crime in this country.

Promo 10” Security companies are there to protect us and our belongings, but sometimes they falter, and even become the prime suspect in the very crime they were supposed to protect us from...
Promo 15” "Three business owners in Bedfordview, Johannesburg suspect their security company or its staff had something to do with the break-ins at their properties...

Jacqui:
Really, I think he's delusional when he thinks that there is not a conspiracy going on within his company. "
Promo 15” "Who is number one on your suspect list after a burglary?

O'Raffety:
It is typical for people to blame the security man, automatically – evidence or no evidence.

V/O:
But is it simply a knee-jerk reaction, or are three Johannesburg business owners indeed victims of insider crime?"
